C1.source: Read Sections3.1-3.3 pp.4-6, Figure1 caption p.7, Bloch Eqs.(4)-(6) p.12 and masking/non-recurrent caveat p.13.
C1.independent_argument: Substitute M=(0,0,+/-M0), B=(b,0,B0) into printed Bloch equations: both transverse rewards are zero, but My derivatives are +/-gamma b M0 and Mz derivatives 0 or 2M0/T1. Thus the observed proxy alone cannot identify equilibrium recovery. For iid Gaussian x/y readout noise, the squared norm has survival exp(-z/(2sigma^2)); integrating the maximum survival gives 2sigma^2 H_N. Expanding Var(sum Xi/n) gives sigma^2/n+2 sum cov/n^2, hence sigma^2[.1+.9/100]=.109sigma^2 for the illustrative equicorrelated case.
C1.hypotheses_and_alternatives: The Gaussian maximum and equicorrelation examples are explicitly special-case diagnostics, not estimates of actual noise bias or proof of correlated electronic noise. Source p.6 permits partial resets and p.13 acknowledges masked state; a calibrated non-equilibrium cycle can be valid. Figure1 reports five seeds and five environments, so evidence is not falsely described as single-run or absent.
C1.dependency_severity_and_repair: Needs Evidence retained for equal-error total acquisition speedup only. The 16% sentence compares peak attainment against completion of the baseline pulse, not a supplied held-out concentration-error/time curve. No simulated result is refuted, no repaired policy is proposed, and full equilibrium is not required if a calibrated partial-reset protocol supplies the missing evidence.
